newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire's foreign minister feared killed - diplomats.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's foreign minister feared killed - diplomats.

text.p: Western diplomats in Zaire's capital Kinshasa said they feared Foreign Minister Kamanda wa Kamanda had been shot dead on Saturday by one of his own bodyguards.
Diplomats from three embassies and some Zairean sources said Kamanda was killed as he tried to leave Kinshasa by boat to neighbouring Congo. Rebels entered the city early on Saturday.
"The information we have is that Kamanda was killed at the Beach (port) early in the morning," said one diplomat. Other diplomats had the same information.
Neither Kamanda nor his wife were answering their cellular telephones on Saturday.

Kamanda, who was also deputy prime minister, was at the forefront of veteran president Mobutu Sese Seko's team in negotiations with the rebels. A polished lawyer with a sharp intellect, he survived numerous government reshuffles.
Diplomats saw him as one figure in the government who tried to ensure a "soft landing" for Laurent Kabila's rebels as defeat of Mobutu's ragged army loomed.

Reports of his death coincided with eyewitness accounts suggesting that hardline Mobutu loyalists were turning on prominent members of the government who favoured some sort of accommodation with the rebels.
Mobutu's elite presidential guard, built largely from his Ngbandi tribe, was on Saturday blamed by diplomats for the killing of army chief of staff General Mahele Lieko Bokungu.
Mobutu on Friday left Kinshasa for the palace he built in the jungle at his ancestral village of Gbadolite.
Kamanda was one of Africa's most experienced diplomats and at one time served as a deputy secretary-general of the Organisation of African Unity (OAU).
